method: Independent recomputation in Node (stdlib, BigInt) from the nine raw records.jsonl files, written without reading research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/analysis/evaluate.mjs and without opening results.json, results.md, summary.json or band/ until own-numbers.json was written (stage 1: validator/compute.mjs; stage 2: validator/report.mjs compares with the producer's numbers taken from the frozen-commit blobs). Pricing per AGENTS.md section 5a and the documented formula of src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/band.rs, priced_gae(w) = G - C + w (U + n_C) with C, n_C from the phase `native` counters priced by docs/ic/calibration.json's pinned row, U = cost.unpriced counts (+ counted table_insert_attempts), checked by the integrality of G - C on every IC record. Certificates re-verified by affine scalar multiplication [recovered]G = target on every record (warm-ups included). Ratios are sums of counted cost over (workload, round) pairs of the three replicates; intervals from 4,000 stratified resamples (seed 20261002). Order of work, disclosed: compute.mjs was first run and own-numbers.json first written before results.json, results.md, summary.json and band/ were opened (I looked at them only after); compute.mjs was then re-run several times, but only to ADD checks and sensitivities (spec identity-view reproduction, automorphism/integrality/marker counts, recorded-GAE and exact-sum sensitivities, per-incumbent per-scope upper ends); no ratio, pricing or pairing code path changed after the producer's numbers were seen, and a copy of own-numbers.json that another session committed mid-run carries the same pooled ratios (checks.regeneration_witness_committed_intermediate_own_numbers). I made no commits.

checks.disposition_note: Gate status concerns the recomputation, identity, registration and certificates. Whether L1 holds is separate (checks.l1).

certificates.method: affine double-and-add over F_p with BigInt: [recovered]G == target, recovered in [0, r), target on curve, generator on curve with [r]G = O; every record including warm-ups; independent of ecbench and of the solvers
certificates.out_of_scope: target derivation (hash_to_subgroup_v1) was not re-derived; the certificate shows each answer is a discrete log of the recorded target

intervals.note: stratified by session; draws: (workload, round) pairs (pair bootstrap) or workloads (cluster bootstrap); percentile interval, type-7 quantiles; PRNG splitmix32 stream
intervals.primary_for_rule: pair_bootstrap (as dispatched); cluster_bootstrap and delta_method reported as sensitivity

l1.rule_text: upper end of the 95% interval of R_w below 1 at w=0,0.1,1, pooled and in each of the 3 replicate sessions alone, and 1 - max_w upper(R_w, pooled) > delta - 1 with delta at w=0
l1.statement: ksum5 costs 0.426-0.691 of the strictest incumbent arm I(w) (pair-table recipe, strictest of the inc-* arms) over the nine curve x weight cells; the largest pair-bootstrap upper end over all pooled and per-replicate scopes is 0.7263 (P20/w0/r2); ksum5 is 5.603-6.851x matched negation rho and 6.100-7.160x bsgs-neg (distance remaining). This is an improvement of the index-calculus incumbent, not a beat of rho.

recorded_baseline_in_prime_base_size_com.reading: relabelling (falls at w = 0, rises at w = 1); incumbent kept

hazards.text: The checkout moved while this validation ran. HEAD values I observed, in order: 6860852096 (my first command), af76d7dfda, 3eee66d158, then 7bcddf781b97ee4074bcdeaf6f4e7d21e4e001fc at the start of the final compute.mjs and 7bcddf781b97ee4074bcdeaf6f4e7d21e4e001fc at the end of the final report.mjs; the producer was committing in the same working tree (untracked benchmarks/20261115-tableb-ksum/ and modified scripts/build_ic_leaderboard.py were present when I looked). Validation is bound to commit 6860852096c10585ea76085486d24df3ec758795 (it lands the sessions, results.json, band/ and the replay certificate). Every consumed committed file (45 files) was compared with its 6860852096c10585ea76085486d24df3ec758795 blob at the start and again at the end (identical at end: true); the nine records.jsonl are bound by sha256 and byte count to the committed .artifacts.json (identical at end: true). Paths under the study directory that differ between 6860852096c10585ea76085486d24df3ec758795 and HEAD and were not consumed: research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/analysis/plot.mjs, research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/analysis/summary.mjs, research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/l1-ratios.svg, research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/replay-local.sh, research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/report.pdf, research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/report.typ, research/ic_tableb_ksum_20261115/summary.json. Paths under validator/ that HEAD already contains (6 files, committed by someone else while I was working, not by me): their committed copies are intermediate versions; the files on disk are final and pinned by validator_files_sha256 in this report.

records.jsonl (9 x ~14 MB) is gitignored and lives in the artifact store; the repository holds only .artifacts.json (sha256, bytes). raw_data paths resolve in this hydrated checkout and hash correctly, but a clean clone without `tools/artifacts pull` has no raw data, while docs/VALIDATION_GATE.md asks for raw data 'in the repository'.

session.json carries git_commit=null and git_dirty=null in all 9 sessions; code identity rests on binary sha256 7d46e5ee... (BINARY.sha256, matches every session.json and every record) and the claim that it was built from src-7b3c057e1c.tgz (sha256 3d61948e..., not in the repository). The binary-to-source link was not rebuilt or verified (a rebuild is outside this validator's remit). Pricing-relevant sources are identical between the claimed source commit 7b3c057e1c and 6860852096c10585ea76085486d24df3ec758795 (git diff --stat empty for band.rs, calibration.json, methods.rs, record.rs, solver_units.rs: yes, empty), so reading band.rs from this tree is a reading of the code the binary's band used; the band JSON of the producer also reproduces from my arithmetic (cross_check.max_rel_diff_band_json_mean_S_vs_validator).

w=0 for the incumbents and k-sum arms is not the recorded cost.s. The band strips the calibration-priced native counters (lookups, target_guard_probes, row_ops, sqrt_solves, legendre_symbols, inversions) out of total_gae (G - C) and charges them at w, so R_0 charges group additions and doublings only and native lookups etc. enter only at w > 0. The ratios on the recorded total_gae (calibration-priced, not the band) are in checks.sensitivity.*.recorded_total_gae_ksum5_over_each_incumbent_pooled and are also below 1. Evidence that the calibration row used for C is the right one: G - C is an integer for all 8640 IC records (measured and warm-up) of the 9 sessions (non-integral: 0, largest fractional part 1.46e-11); the canary in selftest.out shows a neighbouring curve's row makes it non-integral on every record. The w > 0 pricing is not derivable from a spec file alone: I implemented the formula of band.rs's module comment, priced_gae(w) = G - C + w (U + n_C), and the producer's ecbench band JSON (frozen blob) agrees with my sums exactly (cross_check).

The band charges only table_insert_attempts (behind its marker) from work_native; every other counted work_native counter (walk_modr_adds, walk_mix_hashes, target_rng_draws, row_build_*, gauss_entries_scanned, index_*, oracle lookups, and rho's cycle_window_word_ops) is charged at no weight on any arm. Mean uncharged work_native ops per measured run (ksum5 / best incumbent / rho-neg) per curve are in checks.sensitivity.stress_price_all_work_native. ksum5/I stays well below 1 under (a) the complete bitop/v1 unit and (b) a stress reading that prices all of it at w (pooled ksum5 / each incumbent 0.389-0.590 at w=0.1 and 0.285-0.425 at w=1); but the gap to rho is NOT robust to (b): ksum5/rho-neg falls from 5.603-6.851 (band) to 3.012-3.153 (w=0.1) and 1.354-1.453 (w=1) because rho-neg also carries large uncharged cycle_window_word_ops. Under bitop/v1 the gap is 5.622, 5.656, 5.792 (consistent with the band). The registered claim is ksum5/I only; the distance-to-rho number depends on the pricing reading and a stress price of 1 GAE per word op is not a calibrated figure.

rho-neg and rho-neg-aa have identical records within every session (576 of 576 measured+warm-up records per curve identical in total_gae, counters and recovered scalar), as PROTOCOL.md section 3 says; they carry no noise information. The noise floor delta is the across-replicate spread of an arm's mean S, which is what the rule uses (delta at w=0: P20: 1.0392 (inc-tb), P22: 1.0521 (inc-tb), P24: 1.0623 (rho-neg)).

I(w) is chosen on the same data it is compared on, which can only raise R_w (favours the incumbent). The choice is nearly a tie: second-best over best incumbent is 1.003-1.061; at P20 the per-replicate argmin differs between replicates (inc-sel, inc-tb, inc-sel at w=0 and 0.1). Leave-one-replicate-out selection (choose I on two replicates, evaluate on the third) gives held-out ratios within 0.0200 of the in-sample per-replicate ratios (largest at P20/w0/r2) and always < 1 (max held-out ratio 0.6876) (checks.recompute.*.leave_one_replicate_out). ksum5 is cheaper than EVERY incumbent arm at every w in every curve (ksum5_over_each_incumbent_pooled, all < 1: true), so the verdict does not depend on which incumbent is called I.

results.json 'pairs: 144' for a pooled ratio and 'pairs: 48' per replicate count workloads (clusters), not run pairs: the pooled ratio is a ratio of sums over 432 (workload, round) pairs (144 per session). My nine pooled ratios equal the producer's with maximum relative difference 0.0e+0, so the sums are over the same 432 pairs. Producer's reported 'max upper (both intervals)' is the larger of its linearised-t and its two-stage-bootstrap upper ends; I report pair-bootstrap (registered in the dispatch), workload-cluster bootstrap and the delta-method interval, all computed independently (checks.recompute).

Sessions ran on a RunPod CPU pod with the machine busy (load average 37-45 in data/runlog-pod.tsv) under --allow-busy and isolation level L0 (wall times are L0 diagnostics; no wall time is claimed and none was validated). Counted cost is host-independent; replays on a second host (replay-certificate.json) were not reviewed by this validator beyond the requirement that it exist.

No record is censored, unverified, exhausted, zero-cost or lacking a cost; no arm has a missing count (every unpriced counter named by a record carries its count); every IC record carries the counted:table_insert_attempts marker (432 of 432 measured IC records per arm per curve), so table inserts are charged on every IC arm alike; warm-up records (384 per session, round 0) are excluded from all statistics and verified separately (certificates, seals).

AGENTS.md 'Implementation language: no Python' says verifiers should be Rust by default. This validator is Node (stdlib, BigInt curve arithmetic), as the dispatch allowed and as the study's own scripts are; it is not Python and not Rust. Exploratory one-off inspections of the first records in this session used throwaway Python one-liners; no number in the report comes from them.
